market_holds: Spot 42.96 at 18:09 UTC on 2026-11-19 (sealed baseline). The stock is 23% below its 52-week high and 35% above its low; 5-day run-up +5.6%, 20-day -6.0%; 20-day realised vol 47% annualised, so an ordinary day is about 3%. Options (Dec-18 expiry, ATM spread 31% of mid, so illiquid) price a 23.9% event move, 14 vol points of put skew and put/call open interest of 4.3: the market is paying for downside. Short interest 20.1m shares, 6.8 days to cover (settlement 2026-09-30). Consensus (Earnings Whispers): Q3 revenue $739.4m, which is exactly the midpoint of the company's 2026-08-13 guide ($733-745m), and so leaves out Airtable, closed 2026-09-04. FY2026 revenue consensus is about $2.88B against a company guide of $2.78-2.82B (EW and a 2026-11-15 preview). Adjusted EPS consensus is $0.26-0.32 against $0.46 reported in Q2. The Q3 adjusted operating income (AOI) guide is $380-400m. A sell-side bear (BofA, Underperform, PT $38) said in a note dated about 2026-11-16 that buy-side expectations for Q3 revenue and AOI have fallen 'significantly' below the guide on AI-disruption fears. Hedgeye has it as a short. Only one prior print: on 2026-08-13 the stock fell 16.5% (48.98 to 40.92), even though Q2 beat consensus on revenue ($704m vs $684-685m) and on EPS ($0.46 vs $0.24-0.27). Coverage blamed the FY revenue guide coming in below the Street (and 3% organic growth), after a +43% run-in the week before. This time there is no such run-in. Since 2026-10-28 BSP is down 8.6%, against software (IGV) down 13.4%, and over the last 5 sessions it is up 5.6% while IGV fell 4.4%.
view: This print carries a near-mechanical change in the headline that the stale consensus does not reflect. The August guide was 'based solely on businesses owned as of August 12'. Since then BSP has closed Airtable (2026-09-04, about $480m ARR) and Miro (2026-10-26, about $600m ARR), and it said Miro will be added to the outlook at this report. So Q3 revenue should include about four weeks of Airtable, roughly $35m on my arithmetic, against a consensus sitting at the ex-Airtable guide midpoint. The new FY outlook should include Airtable for Q4 (about $120m) and about two months of Miro (about $110m). On the company's own ex-M&A Q4 implied by its guide (about $756m), that gives a FY near $3.0-3.07B against a $2.88B consensus. The Street's figure implies a Q4 of about $835m, which looks like partial Airtable and no Miro. That is the exact reverse of August, when a FY guide that excluded Airtable read as 'below estimates' and the stock fell about 17%. A newly listed company also builds its first guides with a cushion: management said it 'incorporated some revenue disruption' for the AOL ad-tech rebuild and that Q2 organic 'came in a little higher than we expected'. And a bear on the stock says the buy-side bar sits below the guide. Add a downside-heavy options book, and the headline package (revenue beat, EPS beat, FY raised above the Street) leans up. What decides whether that survives to 13:00 ET is the line I cannot see: organic growth (6% in Q1, 3% in Q2, with Remini and Splice declining) and what the call says about AI exposure and Q4 AOI. That includes margin dilution from 'investing substantially' in Airtable and Miro, and interest on about $3B of new debt (a $1.25B + EUR395m term loan B add-on closed 2026-10-02; $1.8B of notes at 9.625%/8.625% priced 2026-10-28). Sophisticated holders know the added revenue was bought with debt, and the tape for software is weak. I lean up, at a strength short of a recommendation.
unpriced: Consensus is stale on M&A that has already closed. Q3 revenue consensus ($739.4m) equals the ex-Airtable guide midpoint, and FY consensus ($2.88B) appears to lack Miro. So the release's headline revenue and FY outlook will print well above 'estimates', on the same headline line that drove the last reaction. Add a buy-side bar reported to sit below the company's own guide and a downside-heavy options book. The bias is stale estimates plus over-extrapolation of the last reaction. It is only partly unpriced, because informed holders can do this arithmetic. The real gap is in how the headline is read, not in the information.

recommendation.reason: The mechanism is clear: consensus excludes two acquisitions already closed, so the headline revenue and the FY outlook should print above estimates. That reverses the FY-vs-Street line that sank the August print, against a buy-side bar reported below guide and bearish options positioning. But the line serious holders will trade on by 13:00 ET is organic growth and the AI and Remini commentary, and I cannot see its inputs. The trend is decelerating (6% to 3%), so a flat or negative organic number could overwhelm the headline. That keeps the probability below the 65 needed to act.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Organic revenue growth reported at or below 0%, with Remini or other app declines widening, or a Q4 AOI outlook that implies sharp margin dilution from Airtable and Miro. Either would turn the M&A-inflated FY raise into a 'bought growth, shrinking core' story.

self_critique: The August fall may have been mostly a run-up unwind (+43% in a week, then -8% the day before), with the FY gap as the excuse. If so, a mechanically higher FY headline need not lift the stock this time. Informed holders know Airtable and Miro are revenue bought with about $3B of debt at junk coupons, and they will look straight to organic growth, which is decelerating and exposed to Remini and AI fears. A 0% or negative organic print, or a weak Q4 AOI margin, could produce another double-digit fall. The headline itself will say the outlook includes Miro, which blunts the 'beat' framing. Software is in a 13% three-week drawdown and BSP is high beta, so tomorrow's tape alone can swamp a few points. These keep me short of 65 but do not reverse the lean: the bar is reported to sit below the guide, and positioning is bearish.
